traps.why: Chromic acid does not stop at the aldehyde: in water the aldehyde hydrates and is oxidised again to the acid. PCC is the reagent that stops.

explanation: A 1° alcohol is oxidised past the aldehyde to the carboxylic acid by chromic acid.
tip: Jones on a 1° alcohol: all the way to COOH.

traps.why: Jones does not break C–C bonds. A 2° alcohol stops at the ketone because there is no H left on the carbonyl carbon.
Dehydration is H₂SO₄/heat without an oxidant. Chromic acid oxidises the alcohol instead.
2° alcohols do react: they give ketones. Only 3° alcohols are inert to chromic acid.

explanation: A 2° alcohol is oxidised to the ketone and stops there. PCC would give the same product.

explanation: Both 1° alcohols are oxidised to carboxylic acids: pentanedioic acid.
tip: Two CH₂OH groups, two COOH groups.
